A1.justification: Both complete, readable 20-page PDFs describe the same MoGaF work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplements support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original forecasting, interpolation, tracking, and ablation results on iPhone and D-NeRF, including supplementary experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds observation-ratio results and a quantitative Gaussian-grouping comparison.

M1.justification: Section 4 and supplementary Sections A–B retain the same grouping algorithms, rigid/non-rigid motion objectives, masked Transformer forecaster, and autoregressive inference. Wording and cross-reference edits do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: The datasets, represented scenes, and forecasting/interpolation/tracking tasks remain unchanged. The additional iPhone observation ratios change splits within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Gaga-4D, already present in qualitative grouping comparisons in Figures 3 and 8, newly participates in the quantitative forecasting comparison in v2 Table 7b. The existing forecasting and interpolation comparators are retained.

E3.justification: V2 Section C.1 and Table 4 add 70%/30% and 90%/10% observation/forecast splits for iPhone, alongside the existing 60%/40% and 80%/20% evaluations. Existing metrics and stated component-ablation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section D.2 and Table 7b test how motion-aware grouping versus Gaga-4D affects forecasting, using photometric and tracking metrics under the existing 60%/40% setting. The optimization, forecasting, capacity, and masking ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. Added results retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Forecast-tracking results are substantially revised throughout Table 3a and v1 Table 6/v2 Table 7a. Under the same stated setting, MoGaF's EPE changes from 0.220 to 0.236, AJ from 27.3 to 17.5, and OA from 79.0 to 80.1, without an explanation for the replacements. V2 Tables 4 and 7b add observation-ratio and grouping results. Main forecasting Tables 1–2 and interpolation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The transmittance definition following Equation (2) corrects the opacity subscript from alpha_n to alpha_j, matching the product index j. This is a localized mathematical correction; the remaining formulations and derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about structured Gaussian grouping, motion optimization, lightweight forecasting, and improved long-term scene extrapolation. Additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New Section D.2 attributes forecasting gains to better separation of coherent motion and discusses OOD extrapolation. The relocated limitations retain reconstruction and collision concerns while adding proposed remedies involving point-cloud completion, generative priors, and physically grounded Gaussian representations.

D1.justification: Supplementary Section B retains the same initialization budget, grouping parameters, reassignment rules, loss weights, forecaster architecture, and masking schedule. The project-page access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 52 works and retain the same related-work discussion and positioning relative to Gaussian reconstruction, segmentation, and forecasting methods. Additional Gaga-4D evaluation supports an existing distinction.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and cross-reference corrections, adds acknowledgements, moves component analysis from C.3 to D.1, and relocates revised limitations to supplementary Section E. The main narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns Figure 1, relocates Figures 7 and 9 and Table 3, adds Table 4, and expands the component table into Table 7a–b. Supplementary typography and table highlighting change, while the remaining qualitative figures are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 7b adds direct quantitative validation of the grouping choice previously supported mainly visually, and Table 4 broadens validation across observation ratios. These additions modestly strengthen the empirical case. The benefit is tempered by unexplained replacements of the tracking-ablation scores; those numerical changes themselves cannot be treated as improved quality.
